Baraitser-Winter Cerebrofrontofacial Syndrome

Mendelian MONDO:0017579 Pathograph 106 Show in embeddings browser Rare neurodevelopmental syndrome Cortical malformation syndrome

Baraitser-Winter cerebrofrontofacial syndrome is an autosomal dominant developmental actinopathy caused by heterozygous missense variants in ACTB or ACTG1, usually arising de novo. Its variable manifestations include distinctive craniofacial features, ocular coloboma, cortical malformations, developmental impairment, hearing loss, and musculoskeletal, cardiac, renal, or gastrointestinal abnormalities. Functional consequences depend on the allele and experimental system. Human cerebral organoids support a progenitor-division mechanism for microcephaly, while epithelial experiments with ACTB Ser348Leu support a possible pathway to orofacial clefting; these models do not establish one cellular mechanism for every manifestation.

Subtypes

2
Baraitser-Winter syndrome 1 (ACTB) MONDO:0009470
ACTB hgnc:132 HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee (hgnc) Relation: this subtype is caused by variation in this gene This subtype is caused by variation in ACTB (hgnc:132). hgnc:132 is a gene from the HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee.
ACTB-related disease caused by heterozygous missense variants with dominant effects on actin function. Most cases arise de novo. Severe presentations formerly called Fryns-Aftimos syndrome fall within this spectrum, but severity varies between alleles and between individuals carrying the same allele.
Baraitser-Winter syndrome 2 (ACTG1) MONDO:0013812
ACTG1 hgnc:144 HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee (hgnc) Relation: this subtype is caused by variation in this gene This subtype is caused by variation in ACTG1 (hgnc:144). hgnc:144 is a gene from the HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee.
ACTG1-related disease caused by heterozygous missense variants. Cortical malformations are frequent in reported BRWS cohorts, with marked variation in severity. ACTG1-related nonsyndromic hearing loss DFNA20/26 is an allelic condition and should not be counted as BRWS solely because the same gene is involved.

Mechanistic Hypotheses

2
Altered progenitor division and microcephaly
organoid_progenitor_depletion EMERGING
Evidence balance 2 support
Patient-derived ACTB Thr120Ile and ACTG1 Thr203Met cerebral organoids, supported by engineered ACTB Thr120Ile organoids, link abnormal progenitor division orientation to reduced ventricular-zone progenitor abundance. Delamination and long-term neuronal-output effects are inferred, and the upstream contribution of individual cytoskeletal abnormalities remains unresolved.

Variant-Dependent Actin Cytoskeletal Dysregulation -> Apical Progenitor Cytoskeletal Irregularities INDIRECT UNKNOWN INTERMEDIATES ACTB Thr120Ile and ACTG1 Thr203Met organoids display apical structural abnormalities; the lymphoblastoid drug response is not itself the demonstrated intermediate.
Apical Progenitor Cytoskeletal Irregularities -> Actin-Dependent Apical Progenitor Cleavage-Plane Defect UNKNOWN Apical cytoskeletal and morphological abnormalities may alter spindle positioning; the study expressly does not establish their causal relationship.
Actin-Dependent Apical Progenitor Cleavage-Plane Defect -> Reduced Ventricular-Zone Progenitor Abundance INDIRECT KNOWN INTERMEDIATES The orientation shift is proposed to increase delamination and basal progenitor output at the expense of the apical progenitor pool.
Reduced Ventricular-Zone Progenitor Abundance -> Microcephaly INDIRECT UNKNOWN INTERMEDIATES An early reduction in the primary progenitor pool may limit later neuronal output and brain growth. This explanation is supported by smaller organoids and microcephaly in the donors, not direct measurement of fetal patient progenitor dynamics.
Show evidence (2 references)
PMID:41372632 SUPPORT PRIMARY RESULT In Vitro
"We found that in contrast to the predominantly vertical cleavage plane orientation of mitotic APs in control cerebral organoids, mitotic APs of BWCFF-S cerebral organoids exhibited a nearly randomized or majoritarian horizontal cleavage plane orientation"
This is the directly observed division-orientation phenotype in ACTB Thr120Ile and ACTG1 Thr203Met patient-derived organoids.
PMID:41372632 SUPPORT INDIRECT PRIMARY RESULT In Vitro
"the VZ progenitor pool in BWCFF-S cerebral organoids is diminished, likely due to the shift in cleavage plane orientation of mitotic anaphase APs, which increases the probability of progenitor delamination and thereby promotes BP generation at the expense of the primary progenitor type, the AP."
The authors infer the orientation-to-delamination mechanism from static division angles and increased basal progenitor abundance; daughter-cell fate was not directly traced.
ACTB Ser348Leu epithelial dysfunction and clefting
ser348leu_epithelial_clefting EMERGING
Evidence balance 1 support
Reduced PFN1 association, impaired junctional localization, and slower migration in overexpression models suggest an epithelial contribution to clefting with ACTB Ser348Leu. Partial PFN1 rescue concerns localization in cultured cells. The frog indel phenotype and failure of mutant ACTB to rescue it do not reproduce the exact human heterozygous genotype.
Pathograph links

Reduced ACTB-PFN1 Association -> Impaired Junctional ACTB Localization DIRECT PFN1 coexpression partially restores mutant junctional localization, supporting a contribution of the impaired interaction.
Impaired Junctional ACTB Localization -> Reduced Epithelial Cell Migration UNKNOWN Defective junctional localization and slower gap closure occur in the same mutant overexpression system; their causal sequence is proposed rather than isolated experimentally.
Reduced Epithelial Cell Migration -> Orofacial Cleft INDIRECT UNKNOWN INTERMEDIATES Impaired epithelial behavior is proposed to contribute to clefting for ACTB Ser348Leu; the cell assay does not directly demonstrate human palatal fusion.

How faithfully do human iPSC-derived ACTB/ACTG1 cerebral organoids explain the full in vivo Baraitser-Winter cortical malformation spectrum, including pachygyria/lissencephaly, anterior-predominant gradients and genotype-specific ACTB versus ACTG1 severity?
HUMAN MODEL MISMATCH OPEN gap_bwcff_organoid_to_human_cortical_malformation_fidelity
Attached to
pathophysiology#Variant-Dependent Actin Cytoskeletal Dysregulation pathophysiology#Cortical Developmental Malformation pathophysiology#Actin-Dependent Apical Progenitor Cleavage-Plane Defect
The published organoid study establishes altered progenitor orientation and abundance, including replication in engineered ACTB Thr120Ile organoids. It does not show that this mechanism reproduces the complete human cortical migration pattern, anteroposterior gradient, or variant-specific severity. Patient-variant correction, ACTG1 isogenic comparisons, and later cortical organization remain useful tests.

Pathophysiology

Dominant ACTB or ACTG1 Missense Actinopathy
Heterozygous ACTB or ACTG1 missense variants alter cytoplasmic actin function. Dominant-negative or gain-of-function effects are supported; a uniform increase in actin stability and simple haploinsufficiency are not established mechanisms for classic BRWS.

Show evidence (3 references)
PMID:22366783 SUPPORT PRIMARY RESULT Human Clinical
"Using whole-exome sequencing of three proband-parent trios, we identified de novo missense changes in the cytoplasmic actin-encoding genes ACTB and ACTG1 in one and two probands, respectively."
Establishes that de novo missense mutations in cytoplasmic actin genes ACTB and ACTG1 are the molecular cause of Baraitser-Winter syndrome.
PMID:22366783 SUPPORT PRIMARY RESULT Human Clinical
"Sequencing of both genes in 15 additional affected individuals identified disease-causing mutations in all probands, including two recurrent de novo alterations (ACTB, encoding p.Arg196His, and ACTG1, encoding p.Ser155Phe)."
The founding study found an ACTB or ACTG1 missense variant in each of 18 selected probands; this is a cohort finding, not proof of universal de novo inheritance.
PMID:22366783 SUPPORT PRIMARY RESULT In Vitro
"Several observations support a dominant-negative or gain-of-function mechanism for the disease-causing mutations."
The founding study supports an altered-function dominant mechanism rather than simple haploinsufficiency, without resolving one universal biochemical direction.
Variant-Dependent Actin Cytoskeletal Dysregulation
Patient lymphoblastoid cells show mutation-specific F-actin accumulation and abnormal morphology. ACTB Arg196His confers relative latrunculin resistance whereas ACTG1 Ser155Phe increases sensitivity. Other variants and tissues can show different biochemical behavior; organoids do not show a corresponding uniform increase in actin abundance.

PMID:22366783 SUPPORT PRIMARY RESULT In Vitro
"We observed an increased resistance to latrunculin A in β-actin p.Arg196His mutant cells, which is consistent with the previously reported p.Arg183Trp mutation34, whereas the γ-actin p.Ser155Phe mutant displayed increased sensitivity to the treatment"
Patient-derived lymphoblastoid cells show opposite drug sensitivities for these two alleles; increased filament stability is not a uniform consequence of BRWS variants.
Apical Progenitor Cytoskeletal Irregularities
Patient-derived cerebral organoids show variable apical cell shape, intercellular protrusions, and increased apical microtubule bundles. The adherens-junction belt is largely preserved and astral microtubule counts are unchanged. These observations are candidate contributors to altered spindle positioning rather than proven individual causes.

PMID:41372632 SUPPORT PRIMARY RESULT In Vitro
"we observed a higher density of microtubule bundles at the apical cell cortex that appeared to be anchored to the apical adherens junction belt rather than being nucleated at the basal body of the primary cilium"
Electron microscopy identifies abnormal apical cytoskeletal organization in the patient-derived organoids. The authors did not quantify these ultrastructural changes or establish their causal relation to spindle orientation.
Actin-Dependent Apical Progenitor Cleavage-Plane Defect
ACTB Thr120Ile and ACTG1 Thr203Met patient-derived cerebral organoids show a shift away from predominantly vertical apical-progenitor cleavage planes. Engineered heterozygous ACTB Thr120Ile organoids reproduce this finding. Cleavage angle constrains possible division modes but does not by itself determine daughter-cell fate.

PMID:41372632 SUPPORT PRIMARY RESULT In Vitro
"We found that in contrast to the predominantly vertical cleavage plane orientation of mitotic APs in control cerebral organoids, mitotic APs of BWCFF-S cerebral organoids exhibited a nearly randomized or majoritarian horizontal cleavage plane orientation"
This is the directly observed division-orientation phenotype in ACTB Thr120Ile and ACTG1 Thr203Met patient-derived organoids.
Reduced Ventricular-Zone Progenitor Abundance
The organoid ventricular zone contains fewer progenitors per ventricle-like structure and is thinner. The basal-progenitor-to-radial-glia ratio is increased; greater basal progenitor production is inferred from these observations. Apoptotic cells remain rare and the proportions of Ki-67- and PH3-positive cells are not significantly different, so progenitor depletion should not be equated with a general cell-cycle arrest.

Show evidence (1 reference)
PMID:41372632 SUPPORT PRIMARY RESULT In Vitro
"quantification of the DAPI-stained nuclei revealed a substantial decrease of the number of VZ progenitors per ventricle-like structure in the BWCFF-S organoids as compared to control organoids"
Direct cell counting documents a smaller ventricular-zone progenitor pool; unchanged Ki-67 and PH3 proportions do not establish a general block in cell cycling.
Cortical Developmental Malformation
Human imaging shows anterior-predominant pachygyria, with less frequent lissencephaly, heterotopia, and corpus-callosum abnormalities. These findings are compatible with disturbed cortical development but do not directly demonstrate a specific neuronal migration, axonal wiring, or regional-timing mechanism. Some affected individuals have no detectable cortical malformation.
Downstream
Pachygyria Pachygyria is a structural manifestation of the cortical developmental disorder.
Intellectual Disability Cortical malformations contribute to neurological impairment, but intellectual disability also occurs with apparently normal MRI.
Seizures Cortical structural abnormalities can contribute to epilepsy; the precise circuit mechanisms are not established by the clinical cohort.

Reduced ACTB-PFN1 Association
ACTB Ser348Leu shows reduced association with exogenous PFN1 in GFP-pulldown experiments from transfected MDCK cells. This allele-specific result suggests altered interactions with an actin-polymerization factor; an equilibrium affinity constant was not measured.

"We detected similar expression levels between the mutant (p.S348L) ... while the signal of PFN1 was noticeably reduced in the sample with mutant ACTB (p.S348L)"

Impaired Junctional ACTB Localization
Overexpressed ACTB Ser348Leu has reduced localization at epithelial cell junctions in MDCK cells and live Xenopus animal-cap epithelium. Diffuse mutant protein does not behave like endogenous filamentous actin during latrunculin treatment. Impaired incorporation is favored, but detailed polymerization effects remain unresolved.

ACTB p.Arg196His
Gene: ACTB hgnc:132 HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee (hgnc) Relation: this variant is in this gene This variant is in ACTB (hgnc:132). hgnc:132 is a gene from the HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee. Missense
A recurrent variant in the founding cohort, reported as NM_001101.2:c.587G>A. Patient-derived cells showed increased F-actin and resistance to latrunculin A.
Show evidence (2 references)
PMID:22366783 SUPPORT PRIMARY RESULT Human Clinical
"Strikingly, 8 patients (44%) carried a mutation disrupting Arg196 of β-actin, including 7 with the same nucleotide change (c.587G>A, p.Arg196His)."
This is recurrence within the 18-person discovery cohort, not a population frequency.
PMID:22366783 SUPPORT PRIMARY RESULT In Vitro
"We observed an increased resistance to latrunculin A in β-actin p.Arg196His mutant cells ... whereas the γ-actin p.Ser155Phe mutant displayed increased sensitivity to the treatment"
Opposite responses to actin-monomer sequestration demonstrate variant-dependent actin dynamics.

Category: Counseling / Informational Action: Genetic CounselingNCI Thesaurus (NCIT) Relation: this treatment is this clinical intervention This treatment is Genetic Counseling (NCIT:C15240). NCIT:C15240 is a clinical intervention from the NCI Thesaurus. NCIT:C15240
Offer parental testing and counseling about autosomal dominant inheritance. Most cases are de novo, but parental germline mosaicism can cause recurrence despite negative parental blood testing. Each child of an affected individual has a 50% chance of inheriting the variant. Prenatal and preimplantation testing are possible once the familial variant is known.

Developmental and Organ Surveillance
Category: Monitoring
Monitor development and educational needs at each visit. Follow seizures as clinically indicated. Provide at least annual ophthalmology with glaucoma screening when coloboma or microphthalmia is present, annual assessment of hearing-loss progression, and at least annual review of feeding/GI dysfunction and scoliosis. Orthopedic review increases to every six months during growth spurts and adolescence; cardiac and renal follow-up depend on existing anomalies.

Assessment of Unexplained Deterioration
Category: Monitoring
Hematologic malignancies have been reported, but an increased syndrome-specific risk is unestablished. GeneReviews recommends evaluation for malignancy when physical deterioration or unexplained chronic fever occurs, and does not recommend regular cancer surveillance.

Diagnosis

3
Molecular Diagnosis
Suggestive clinical findings plus a heterozygous pathogenic or likely pathogenic missense variant in ACTB or ACTG1 establish the diagnosis. Use a relevant multigene panel or exome/genome sequencing according to the presentation. A variant of uncertain significance is not diagnostic; gene deletions or duplications cause different phenotypes.

Differential Diagnoses

5

Conditions with similar clinical presentations that must be differentiated from Baraitser-Winter Cerebrofrontofacial Syndrome:

ACTB-Related Syndromic Thrombocytopenia
Overlapping Features An allelic actinopathy can share developmental delay, microcephaly, facial differences, and malformations.
Distinguishing Features
  • Thrombocytopenia with platelet size variability and clustering of ACTB variants in exons 5–6 distinguish this disorder; thrombocytopenia is not a typical BRWS feature.
Show evidence (1 reference)
url:https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK327153/pdf/Bookshelf_NBK327153.pdf SUPPORT REVIEW SYNTHESIS Human Clinical
"Syndromic thrombocytopenia. Mild DD, mild variable dysmorphism, microcephaly, & leukocytosis as well as thrombocytopenia w/platelet anisotropy"
GeneReviews separates this condition from classic BWCFF syndrome.
ACTB Loss-of-Function Developmental Disorder
Overlapping Features ACTB loss-of-function alleles cause a distinct developmental disorder with overlapping organ malformations.
Distinguishing Features
  • Loss-of-function variants and a different facial pattern should not be treated as the classic BRWS missense mechanism.
Show evidence (1 reference)
url:https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK327153/pdf/Bookshelf_NBK327153.pdf SUPPORT REVIEW SYNTHESIS Human Clinical
"Described in ~40 persons w/DD, ID, internal organ malformations (incl CHDs & renal tract anomalies), growth restriction, & facial dysmorphism distinct from BWCFF syndrome"
GeneReviews separates this condition from classic BWCFF syndrome.
ACTB Arg183Trp Dystonia-Deafness Syndrome
Overlapping Features Historically included in some broad actinopathy series, this allele produces a distinct dystonia-deafness presentation.
Distinguishing Features
  • Drug-nonresponsive dystonia and early-onset sensorineural deafness are characteristic; pooled historical cohorts can distort BRWS natural-history estimates.
Show evidence (1 reference)
url:https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK327153/pdf/Bookshelf_NBK327153.pdf SUPPORT REVIEW SYNTHESIS Human Clinical
"Dystonia-deafness syndrome. Drug-nonresponsive dystonia & early-onset sensorineural deafness"
GeneReviews separates this condition from classic BWCFF syndrome.
ACTG1-Related DFNA20/26
Overlapping Features ACTG1 variants can cause isolated progressive hearing loss without BRWS.
Distinguishing Features
  • A variant in the same gene alone does not establish BRWS; assess the allele and syndromic craniofacial, ocular, and cortical findings.
Show evidence (1 reference)
url:https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK327153/pdf/Bookshelf_NBK327153.pdf SUPPORT REVIEW SYNTHESIS Human Clinical
"Autosomal dominant nonsyndromic progressive sensorineural hearing loss (DFNA20/26)"
GeneReviews separates this condition from classic BWCFF syndrome.
Noonan Syndrome MONDO:0018997
Overlapping Features Ptosis, hypertelorism, chest deformity, and neck webbing can resemble mild BRWS in infancy.
Distinguishing Features
  • Coloboma and pachygyria favor BRWS; coloboma is rare in Noonan syndrome and pachygyria is not a typical feature.

GeneReviews separates this condition from classic BWCFF syndrome.

Experimental Models

4
Patient-Derived Lymphoblastoid Cell Lines CELL_LINE
The founding study tested actin protein abundance, F-actin organization, morphology, and latrunculin A response. ACTB Arg196His and ACTG1 Ser155Phe cells showed increased F-actin but opposite drug responses; actin protein abundance was unchanged. These non-neural cells do not directly establish cortical developmental mechanisms.

Patient-Derived Cerebral Organoids ORGANOID
Patient organoids were compared with SC102A-1 and CRTDi011-A control lines. Mutant organoids were smaller, with altered apical progenitor cleavage orientation and reduced ventricular-zone progenitor abundance. Cytoskeletal abnormalities were observed, but their causal relation to altered division orientation was not established. No patient-variant correction or direct cell-fate tracing was reported.

Engineered ACTB Thr120Ile Cerebral Organoids ORGANOID
Engineered ACTB Thr120Ile organoids provide a comparison in a matched control background and reproduce altered progenitor division orientation and reduced progenitor abundance. These results concern this ACTB allele; an ACTG1 isogenic model and rescue by patient-variant correction were not tested. The number of ventricle-like structures did not differ significantly from controls, unlike the patient-derived comparison.

ACTB Ser348Leu MDCK Epithelial Model CELL_LINE
Mutant ACTB showed reduced junctional localization and slower gap closure. A GFP pull-down from cell lysate mixed with exogenous PFN1 showed reduced association; this was not an equilibrium binding-affinity measurement. PFN1 coexpression partially restored junctional localization. Transient overexpression in canine kidney epithelium does not directly measure human palatal morphogenesis.

Xenopus actb.L/S F0 Crispants
Crispants showed reduced mouth width and intercanthal distance with upper-jaw notching. Wild-type human ACTB supplementation improved these measurements whereas Ser348Leu did not. The model perturbs actin function but does not recreate a heterozygous human missense allele; epithelial migration and PFN1 binding were not measured in these crispants.

name: Baraitser-Winter Cerebrofrontofacial Syndrome
creation_date: '2026-06-05T00:00:00Z'
description: >-
  Baraitser-Winter cerebrofrontofacial syndrome is an autosomal dominant developmental actinopathy caused by
  heterozygous missense variants in ACTB or ACTG1, usually arising de novo. Its variable manifestations include
  distinctive craniofacial features, ocular coloboma, cortical malformations, developmental impairment, hearing
  loss, and musculoskeletal, cardiac, renal, or gastrointestinal abnormalities. Functional consequences depend
  on the allele and experimental system. Human cerebral organoids support a progenitor-division mechanism for
  microcephaly, while epithelial experiments with ACTB Ser348Leu support a possible pathway to orofacial clefting;
  these models do not establish one cellular mechanism for every manifestation.

  description: >-
    Heterozygous ACTB or ACTG1 missense variants alter cytoplasmic actin function. Dominant-negative or gain-of-function
    effects are supported; a uniform increase in actin stability and simple haploinsufficiency are not established
    mechanisms for classic BRWS.

    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Using whole-exome sequencing of three proband-parent trios, we
      identified de novo missense changes in the cytoplasmic actin-encoding
      genes ACTB and ACTG1 in one and two probands, respectively.
    explanation: >-
      Establishes that de novo missense mutations in cytoplasmic actin genes
      ACTB and ACTG1 are the molecular cause of Baraitser-Winter syndrome.
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
  - reference: PMID:22366783
    reference_title: De novo mutations in the actin genes ACTB and ACTG1 cause Baraitser-Winter syndrome.

      encoding p.Ser155Phe).
    explanation: >-

- name: Variant-Dependent Actin Cytoskeletal Dysregulation
  biological_scale: CELLULAR
  biological_processes:
  - preferred_term: actin cytoskeleton organization
    term:
      id: GO:0030036
      label: actin cytoskeleton organization
  description: >-
    Patient lymphoblastoid cells show mutation-specific F-actin accumulation and abnormal morphology. ACTB
    Arg196His confers relative latrunculin resistance whereas ACTG1 Ser155Phe increases sensitivity. Other
    variants and tissues can show different biochemical behavior; organoids do not show a corresponding uniform
    increase in actin abundance.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:22366783
    reference_title: De novo mutations in the actin genes ACTB and ACTG1 cause Baraitser-Winter syndrome.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: >-
      We observed an increased resistance to latrunculin A in β-actin p.Arg196His mutant cells, which is consistent
      with the previously reported p.Arg183Trp mutation34, whereas the γ-actin p.Ser155Phe mutant displayed
      increased sensitivity to the treatment
    explanation: >-
      Patient-derived lymphoblastoid cells show opposite drug sensitivities for these two alleles; increased
      filament stability is not a uniform consequence of BRWS variants.
  downstream:
  - target: Apical Progenitor Cytoskeletal Irregularities
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_UNKNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    description: >-
      ACTB Thr120Ile and ACTG1 Thr203Met organoids display apical structural abnormalities; the lymphoblastoid
      drug response is not itself the demonstrated intermediate.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:41372632
      reference_title: Cerebral organoids expressing mutant actin genes reveal cellular mechanism underlying microcephaly.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      snippet: >-
        we observed a higher density of microtubule bundles at the apical cell cortex that appeared to be anchored
        to the apical adherens junction belt rather than being nucleated at the basal body of the primary cilium
      explanation: >-
        Electron microscopy identifies abnormal apical cytoskeletal organization in the patient-derived organoids.
        The authors did not quantify these ultrastructural changes or establish their causal relation to spindle
        orientation.
    hypothesis_groups:
    - organoid_progenitor_depletion

- name: Actin-Dependent Apical Progenitor Cleavage-Plane Defect
  biological_scale: CELLULAR
  cell_types:
  - preferred_term: ventricular-zone neural progenitor cell
    term:
      id: CL:0011020
      label: neural progenitor cell
  - preferred_term: radial glial progenitor
    term:
      id: CL:0000681
      label: radial glial cell
  description: >-
    ACTB Thr120Ile and ACTG1 Thr203Met patient-derived cerebral organoids show a shift away from predominantly
    vertical apical-progenitor cleavage planes. Engineered heterozygous ACTB Thr120Ile organoids reproduce
    this finding. Cleavage angle constrains possible division modes but does not by itself determine daughter-cell
    fate.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:41372632
    reference_title: Cerebral organoids expressing mutant actin genes reveal cellular mechanism underlying microcephaly.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: >-
      We found that in contrast to the predominantly vertical cleavage plane orientation of mitotic APs in
      control cerebral organoids, mitotic APs of BWCFF-S cerebral organoids exhibited a nearly randomized or
      majoritarian horizontal cleavage plane orientation
    explanation: >-
      This is the directly observed division-orientation phenotype in ACTB Thr120Ile and ACTG1 Thr203Met patient-derived
      organoids.
  downstream:
  - target: Reduced Ventricular-Zone Progenitor Abundance
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_KNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    description: >-
      The orientation shift is proposed to increase delamination and basal progenitor output at the expense
      of the apical progenitor pool.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:41372632
      reference_title: Cerebral organoids expressing mutant actin genes reveal cellular mechanism underlying microcephaly.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      snippet: >-
        the VZ progenitor pool in BWCFF-S cerebral organoids is diminished, likely due to the shift in cleavage
        plane orientation of mitotic anaphase APs, which increases the probability of progenitor delamination
        and thereby promotes BP generation at the expense of the primary progenitor type, the AP.
      explanation: >-
        The authors infer the orientation-to-delamination mechanism from static division angles and increased
        basal progenitor abundance; daughter-cell fate was not directly traced.
      directness: INDIRECT
    hypothesis_groups:
    - organoid_progenitor_depletion
- name: Reduced Ventricular-Zone Progenitor Abundance
  biological_scale: CELLULAR

  - preferred_term: ventricular-zone neural progenitor cell

      id: CL:0011020
      label: neural progenitor cell
  - preferred_term: radial glial progenitor
    term:
      id: CL:0000681
      label: radial glial cell
  description: >-
    The organoid ventricular zone contains fewer progenitors per ventricle-like structure and is thinner. The
    basal-progenitor-to-radial-glia ratio is increased; greater basal progenitor production is inferred from
    these observations. Apoptotic cells remain rare and the proportions of Ki-67- and PH3-positive cells are
    not significantly different, so progenitor depletion should not be equated with a general cell-cycle arrest.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:41372632

    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT

    explanation: >-

- name: Cortical Developmental Malformation
  biological_scale: TISSUE
  description: >-
    Human imaging shows anterior-predominant pachygyria, with less frequent lissencephaly, heterotopia, and
    corpus-callosum abnormalities. These findings are compatible with disturbed cortical development but do
    not directly demonstrate a specific neuronal migration, axonal wiring, or regional-timing mechanism. Some
    affected individuals have no detectable cortical malformation.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:25052316
    reference_title: 'Baraitser-Winter cerebrofrontofacial syndrome: delineation of the spectrum in 42 cases.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Nearly all patients with ACTG1 mutations, and around 60% of those with
      ACTB mutations have some degree of pachygyria with anteroposterior
      severity gradient, rarely lissencephaly or neuronal heterotopia.
    explanation: >-
      The cohort documents the anatomical cortical-malformation pattern. It does not directly measure neuronal
      migration, laminar connectivity, or the origin of the anteroposterior gradient.
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
  - reference: PMID:25052316
    reference_title: 'Baraitser-Winter cerebrofrontofacial syndrome: delineation of the spectrum in 42 cases.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL

      Intellectual disability and epilepsy are variable in severity and
      largely correlate with CNS anomalies.

        largely correlate with CNS anomalies.
      explanation: >-
        The association between neurological severity and CNS malformations supports a contribution of cortical
        pathology, without establishing a specific circuit mechanism or excluding disability with normal MRI.
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
- name: Reduced ACTB-PFN1 Association
  biological_scale: MOLECULAR
  description: >-
    ACTB Ser348Leu shows reduced association with exogenous PFN1 in GFP-pulldown experiments from transfected
    MDCK cells. This allele-specific result suggests altered interactions with an actin-polymerization factor;
    an equilibrium affinity constant was not measured.
  evidence:
  - reference: url:https://ir.library.osaka-u.ac.jp/repo/ouka/all/103591//HumMolGenet_33_22_1975.pdf
    reference_title: https://ir.library.osaka-u.ac.jp/repo/ouka/all/103591//HumMolGenet_33_22_1975.pdf
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: >-
      We detected similar expression levels between the mutant (p.S348L) ... while the signal of PFN1 was noticeably
      reduced in the sample with mutant ACTB (p.S348L)
    explanation: >-
      Tsujimoto et al. (2024), Compromised actin dynamics underlie the orofacial cleft in Baraitser-Winter
      Cerebrofrontofacial Syndrome with a variant in ACTB: GFP pulldown from MDCK extracts mixed with exogenous
      PFN1 shows reduced association. This is not a measured binding constant.
  downstream:
  - target: Impaired Junctional ACTB Localization
    causal_link_type: DIRECT
    description: >-
      PFN1 coexpression partially restores mutant junctional localization, supporting a contribution of the
      impaired interaction.
    evidence:
    - reference: url:https://ir.library.osaka-u.ac.jp/repo/ouka/all/103591//HumMolGenet_33_22_1975.pdf
      reference_title: https://ir.library.osaka-u.ac.jp/repo/ouka/all/103591//HumMolGenet_33_22_1975.pdf
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      snippet: >-
        PFN1 overexpression partially restored the localization of mutated ACTB (p.S348L) to the cell junction
      explanation: >-
        Partial localization rescue supports the proposed interaction-to-localization link in MDCK cells.
    hypothesis_groups:
    - ser348leu_epithelial_clefting
- name: Impaired Junctional ACTB Localization
  biological_scale: CELLULAR
  description: >-
    Overexpressed ACTB Ser348Leu has reduced localization at epithelial cell junctions in MDCK cells and live
    Xenopus animal-cap epithelium. Diffuse mutant protein does not behave like endogenous filamentous actin
    during latrunculin treatment. Impaired incorporation is favored, but detailed polymerization effects remain
    unresolved.
  evidence:
  - reference: url:https://ir.library.osaka-u.ac.jp/repo/ouka/all/103591//HumMolGenet_33_22_1975.pdf
    reference_title: https://ir.library.osaka-u.ac.jp/repo/ouka/all/103591//HumMolGenet_33_22_1975.pdf
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: >-
      In contrast, the mutant ACTB (p.S348L) did not show an intense signal at the cell junction but rather
      showed uniform expression in the cytoplasm
    explanation: >-
      This result is specifically from MDCK cells overexpressing GFP-tagged ACTB.
  downstream:
  - target: Reduced Epithelial Cell Migration
    causal_link_type: UNKNOWN
    description: >-
      Defective junctional localization and slower gap closure occur in the same mutant overexpression system;
      their causal sequence is proposed rather than isolated experimentally.
    evidence:
    - reference: url:https://ir.library.osaka-u.ac.jp/repo/ouka/all/103591//HumMolGenet_33_22_1975.pdf
      reference_title: https://ir.library.osaka-u.ac.jp/repo/ouka/all/103591//HumMolGenet_33_22_1975.pdf
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      snippet: >-
        We observed that the mutant ACTB (p.S348L) -overexpressing cells displayed slower migration over time
        than the wild-type ACTB-overexpressing cells
      explanation: >-
        The MDCK assay measures closure of a defined cell-free gap after removal of a silicone insert. It is
        a surrogate for epithelial behavior, not direct measurement of patient palatal fusion.
    hypothesis_groups:
    - ser348leu_epithelial_clefting
- name: Reduced Epithelial Cell Migration
  biological_scale: CELLULAR
  description: >-
    MDCK cells overexpressing ACTB Ser348Leu close a defined cell-free gap more slowly than cells overexpressing
    wild-type ACTB. This experimental behavior supports a candidate epithelial contribution to clefting rather
    than a directly observed patient palatal-fusion defect.
  evidence:
  - reference: url:https://ir.library.osaka-u.ac.jp/repo/ouka/all/103591//HumMolGenet_33_22_1975.pdf
    reference_title: https://ir.library.osaka-u.ac.jp/repo/ouka/all/103591//HumMolGenet_33_22_1975.pdf
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: >-
      We observed that the mutant ACTB (p.S348L) -overexpressing cells displayed slower migration over time
      than the wild-type ACTB-overexpressing cells
    explanation: >-
      The MDCK assay measures closure of a defined cell-free gap after removal of a silicone insert. It is
      a surrogate for epithelial behavior, not direct measurement of patient palatal fusion.
  downstream:
  - target: Orofacial Cleft
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_UNKNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    hypothesis_groups:
    - ser348leu_epithelial_clefting
    description: >-
      Impaired epithelial behavior is proposed to contribute to clefting for ACTB Ser348Leu; the cell assay
      does not directly demonstrate human palatal fusion.
    evidence:
    - reference: url:https://ir.library.osaka-u.ac.jp/repo/ouka/all/103591//HumMolGenet_33_22_1975.pdf
      reference_title: https://ir.library.osaka-u.ac.jp/repo/ouka/all/103591//HumMolGenet_33_22_1975.pdf
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      snippet: >-
        The limited ability of ACTB(p .S348L) to localize to cell -cell junctions in epithelial cells observed
        in this study may reflect a defect in actin polymerization, consequently impairing surface epithelial
        cell adhesion and palatal shelf convergence in the affected individual ... contributing to the orofacial
        clefting phenotype.
      explanation: >-
        Tsujimoto et al. propose a link from the epithelial findings to clefting. The separate frog experiment
        used mosaic indels near Ser348, not a patient-allele knock-in.
      directness: INDIRECT
phenotypes:
- name: Pachygyria
  description: >-
    Pachygyria is often anterior predominant. The 2015 clinically ascertained cohort reported it in nearly
    all ACTG1 cases and approximately 60% of ACTB cases; these selected-cohort proportions should not be treated
    as invariant gene-specific penetrance.
  category: Neurological
  frequency: FREQUENT
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Pachygyria
    term:
      id: HP:0001302
      label: Pachygyria
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:25052316
    reference_title: 'Baraitser-Winter cerebrofrontofacial syndrome: delineation of the spectrum in 42 cases.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Nearly all patients with ACTG1 mutations, and around 60% of those with
      ACTB mutations have some degree of pachygyria with anteroposterior
      severity gradient, rarely lissencephaly or neuronal heterotopia.
    explanation: >-
      Quantifies pachygyria frequency by subtype in 42 cases, establishing it
      as the primary cortical malformation with characteristic gradient.

- name: Microcephaly
  description: >-
    Microcephaly may be prenatal or develop postnatally. Severity varies, with severe cases accompanying lissencephaly;
    it is not exclusively a secondary postnatal process.
  category: Neurological
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Microcephaly
    term:
      id: HP:0000252
      label: Microcephaly
  evidence:
  - reference: url:https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK327153/pdf/Bookshelf_NBK327153.pdf
    reference_title: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK327153/pdf/Bookshelf_NBK327153.pdf
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: >-
      Microcephaly (~50%) Microcephaly may be of prenatal onset, usually mild, but may be severe w/lissencephaly
    explanation: >-
      GeneReviews, Baraitser-Winter Cerebrofrontofacial Syndrome (March 2022 revision): The chapter reports
      approximately half of affected individuals and explicitly includes prenatal onset.
  frequency: FREQUENT
- name: Intellectual Disability
  description: >-
    Intellectual disability ranges from mild to profound. Structural brain abnormalities influence severity,
    but impairment also occurs with apparently normal brain structure; rare individuals have normal intelligence.
  category: Neurological
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Intellectual disability
    term:
      id: HP:0001249
      label: Intellectual disability
  evidence:
  - reference: url:https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK327153/pdf/Bookshelf_NBK327153.pdf
    reference_title: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK327153/pdf/Bookshelf_NBK327153.pdf
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: >-
      In children with normal brain structure, motor delay is common, but otherwise development is only mildly
      to moderately delayed. ID is usually mild. Rare individuals with normal intelligence have also been reported.
    explanation: >-
      GeneReviews, Baraitser-Winter Cerebrofrontofacial Syndrome (March 2022 revision): The phenotype is common
      but not obligatory; the combined developmental-delay/intellectual-disability percentage is not assigned
      to each component independently.
- name: Seizures
  description: >-
    Epilepsy affects approximately half of reported individuals and varies in type and severity. Onset is age
    dependent, ranging from the first months of life into adulthood. Some seizures are difficult to control,
    but refractoriness is not universal.
  category: Neurological
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Seizures
    term:
      id: HP:0001250
      label: Seizure
  evidence:
  - reference: url:https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK327153/pdf/Bookshelf_NBK327153.pdf
    reference_title: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK327153/pdf/Bookshelf_NBK327153.pdf
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: >-
      Epilepsy, of no specific type and of variable severity, is present in 50% of individuals, often in conjunction
      with structural cerebral anomalies.
    explanation: >-
      GeneReviews, Baraitser-Winter Cerebrofrontofacial Syndrome (March 2022 revision): The chapter supplies
      a patient frequency and explicitly variable severity.
  frequency: FREQUENT
- name: Global Developmental Delay
  description: >-
    Developmental delay varies markedly. Motor and language development may be delayed even when no cortical
    malformation is visible on imaging.
  category: Neurological
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Global developmental delay
    term:
      id: HP:0001263
      label: Global developmental delay
  evidence:
  - reference: url:https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK327153/pdf/Bookshelf_NBK327153.pdf
    reference_title: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK327153/pdf/Bookshelf_NBK327153.pdf
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: >-
      Developmental delay (DD) / intellectual disability (ID) is highly variable: ... In children with normal
      brain structure, motor delay is common
    explanation: >-
      GeneReviews, Baraitser-Winter Cerebrofrontofacial Syndrome (March 2022 revision): The chapter distinguishes
      developmental function from visible brain malformation; its combined DD/ID frequency does not establish
      an isolated global-delay denominator.
- name: Iris Coloboma
  description: >-
    Unilateral or bilateral iris coloboma may occur, sometimes extending into the posterior segment. The roughly
    30% frequency for all ocular coloboma is not an iris-specific estimate.
  category: Ophthalmological
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Iris coloboma
    term:
      id: HP:0000612
      label: Iris coloboma
  evidence:
  - reference: url:https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK327153/pdf/Bookshelf_NBK327153.pdf
    reference_title: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK327153/pdf/Bookshelf_NBK327153.pdf
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: >-
      Uni- or bilateral ocular coloboma that may extend from the iris to the macula, sometimes with microphthalmia
    explanation: >-
      GeneReviews, Baraitser-Winter Cerebrofrontofacial Syndrome (March 2022 revision): This supports iris
      involvement without assigning the combined ocular-coloboma frequency to iris coloboma alone.
- name: Congenital Ptosis
  description: >-
    Bilateral congenital non-myopathic ptosis is a characteristic feature and can require surgery. A specific
    levator-muscle or neural-crest mechanism has not been established by the clinical evidence.
  category: Ophthalmological
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Congenital ptosis
    term:
      id: HP:0000508
      label: Ptosis
  evidence:
  - reference: url:https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK327153/pdf/Bookshelf_NBK327153.pdf
    reference_title: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK327153/pdf/Bookshelf_NBK327153.pdf
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: >-
      Bilateral ptosis (90%) ... Highly arched eyebrows (90%)
    explanation: >-
      GeneReviews, Baraitser-Winter Cerebrofrontofacial Syndrome (March 2022 revision): The chapter gives a
      specific bilateral-ptosis frequency.
  frequency: VERY_FREQUENT
- name: Hypertelorism
  description: >-
    Widely spaced eyes are a highly frequent craniofacial manifestation.
  category: Craniofacial
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Hypertelorism
    term:
      id: HP:0000316
      label: Hypertelorism
  evidence:
  - reference: url:https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK327153/pdf/Bookshelf_NBK327153.pdf
    reference_title: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK327153/pdf/Bookshelf_NBK327153.pdf
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: >-
      Widely spaced eyes (95%) ... Bilateral ptosis (90%)
    explanation: >-
      GeneReviews, Baraitser-Winter Cerebrofrontofacial Syndrome (March 2022 revision): The frequency concerns
      widely spaced eyes directly.
  frequency: VERY_FREQUENT
- name: Trigonocephaly
  description: >-
    Trigonocephaly and a prominent metopic ridge are related but distinct findings. The reported 65% combines
    both and is not a trigonocephaly-specific estimate.
  category: Craniofacial
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Trigonocephaly
    term:
      id: HP:0000243
      label: Trigonocephaly
  evidence:
  - reference: url:https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK327153/pdf/Bookshelf_NBK327153.pdf
    reference_title: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK327153/pdf/Bookshelf_NBK327153.pdf
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: >-
      Prominent metopic ridging or trigonocephaly (65%)
    explanation: >-
      GeneReviews, Baraitser-Winter Cerebrofrontofacial Syndrome (March 2022 revision): The source groups the
      two findings; their frequencies cannot be separated.
- name: Wide Nasal Bridge
  description: >-
    A broad nasal bridge may accompany a broad nose and large tip; these dimensions are recorded separately.
  category: Craniofacial
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Wide nasal bridge
    term:
      id: HP:0000431
      label: Wide nasal bridge
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:25052316
    reference_title: 'Baraitser-Winter cerebrofrontofacial syndrome: delineation of the spectrum in 42 cases.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      hypertelorism, broad nose with large tip and prominent root, congenital
      non-myopathic ptosis, ridged metopic suture and arched eyebrows.
    explanation: >-
      The cohort describes a broad nose and prominent root; the 2014 severe-case series explicitly describes
      a broad nasal bridge. No compound nose frequency is assigned to this individual feature.

  - reference: PMID:23756437
    reference_title: Severe forms of Baraitser-Winter syndrome are caused by ACTB mutations rather than ACTG1 mutations.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: broad nasal bridge, broad nasal tip and columella, anteverted nostrils
    explanation: >-
      The severe-case series documents the bridge and tip separately.
- name: Short Stature
  description: >-
    Moderate short stature is common, with variable prenatal growth.

  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Short stature

  evidence:

    supports: SUPPORT

    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: >-

    explanation: >-
      GeneReviews, Baraitser-Winter Cerebrofrontofacial Syndrome (March 2022 revision): The table assigns 44%

  frequency: FREQUENT
- name: Shoulder Girdle Muscle Atrophy
  description: >-
    Reduced shoulder-girdle muscle bulk and progressive muscle wasting occur in some individuals. Congenital
    muscle hypoplasia and later atrophy are not interchangeable, and the aggregate neuromuscular frequency
    is not a shoulder-specific estimate.
  category: Musculoskeletal
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Shoulder girdle muscle atrophy
    term:
      id: HP:0003724
      label: Shoulder girdle muscle atrophy
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:25052316
    reference_title: 'Baraitser-Winter cerebrofrontofacial syndrome: delineation of the spectrum in 42 cases.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Reduction of shoulder girdle muscle bulk and progressive joint stiffness
      is common. Early muscular involvement, occasionally with congenital
      arthrogryposis, may be present.
    explanation: >-
      Verloes et al. identify shoulder girdle muscle reduction and joint
      stiffness as common features in 42 BRWS cases, with occasional
      arthrogryposis.

- name: Sensorineural Hearing Loss
  description: >-
    Sensorineural hearing impairment may be progressive and require amplification. Conductive hearing loss

  category: Auditory
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Sensorineural hearing loss
    term:

  evidence:

    reference_title: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK327153/pdf/Bookshelf_NBK327153.pdf
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: >-

      aids.
    explanation: >-
      GeneReviews, Baraitser-Winter Cerebrofrontofacial Syndrome (March 2022 revision): This specifically supports
      sensorineural impairment and variable course, without importing frequencies from nonsyndromic ACTG1 deafness.
- name: Congenital Heart Defects
  description: >-

    supports: SUPPORT

    explanation: >-
      GeneReviews, Baraitser-Winter Cerebrofrontofacial Syndrome (March 2022 revision): The chapter reports

- name: Renal Malformations
  description: >-

  category: Renal

    explanation: >-

- name: Gastrointestinal Dysfunction

      disease
    explanation: >-
      GeneReviews, Baraitser-Winter Cerebrofrontofacial Syndrome (March 2022 revision): The frequency applies
      to the broad gastrointestinal spectrum, not to every component.
  frequency: FREQUENT
- name: Retinal Coloboma

  description: >-
    Retinal coloboma varies in extent; visual prognosis depends partly on macular and optic-disc involvement.

- name: Highly Arched Eyebrows

  evidence:
  - reference: url:https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK327153/pdf/Bookshelf_NBK327153.pdf
    reference_title: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK327153/pdf/Bookshelf_NBK327153.pdf
    supports: SUPPORT

    explanation: >-

- name: Prominent Metopic Ridge
  category: Craniofacial

genetic:
- name: ACTB pathogenic missense variants
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: ACTB
    term:
      id: hgnc:132
      label: ACTB
  association: >-
    Heterozygous missense variants with dominant effects on actin function
  relationship_type: CAUSATIVE
  variant_origin: GERMLINE
  subtype: BRWS1
  notes: >-
    Most affected individuals have a de novo variant, but transmission from an affected parent and parental
    germline mosaicism are documented. Penetrance appears complete while no individual clinical feature is
    constant. Functional effects and severity are variant dependent; a gene-level rule that ACTB is always
    more severe than ACTG1 is not established. ACTB loss-of-function and thrombocytopenia-associated alleles
    can cause distinct disorders.
  inheritance:
  - name: Autosomal dominant inheritance
    inheritance_term:
      preferred_term: Autosomal dominant inheritance
      term:
        id: HP:0000006
        label: Autosomal dominant inheritance
  evidence:
  - reference: url:https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK327153/pdf/Bookshelf_NBK327153.pdf
    reference_title: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK327153/pdf/Bookshelf_NBK327153.pdf
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: >-
      Most individuals with BWCFF syndrome reported to date have the disorder as the result of a de novo ACTB
      or ACTG1 pathogenic variant.
    explanation: >-
      GeneReviews (March 2022 revision): Most does not mean all; the following counseling section describes
      inherited and mosaic cases.
  - reference: url:https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK327153/pdf/Bookshelf_NBK327153.pdf
    reference_title: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK327153/pdf/Bookshelf_NBK327153.pdf
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: >-
      In rare families, individuals diagnosed with BWCFF syndrome have the disorder as the result of a pathogenic
      variant inherited from a parent with germline mosaicism
    explanation: >-
      GeneReviews (March 2022 revision): Parental germline mosaicism provides a documented recurrence mechanism.
  - reference: url:https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK327153/pdf/Bookshelf_NBK327153.pdf
    reference_title: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK327153/pdf/Bookshelf_NBK327153.pdf
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: >-
      The penetrance of BWCFF syndrome appears to be complete, but no single clinical manifestation is constant.
    explanation: >-
      GeneReviews (March 2022 revision): The chapter separates syndrome penetrance from feature-specific expressivity.

- name: Cochlear Implantation
  description: >-
    A child with ACTB Ser348Leu-related BRWS received a right cochlear implant after limited hearing-aid benefit.
    Combined implant and contralateral hearing aid improved aided thresholds and tested speech perception;
    spontaneous speech remained difficult to understand. Evidence is a single case, not a comparative trial.
  action_category: THERAPEUTIC
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:38592426
    reference_title: 'Hearing Loss in Baraitser-Winter Syndrome: Case Reports and Review of the Literature.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: >-
      At the age of 2, she was implanted with a Medel Flex 28 CI model.
    explanation: >-
      This is the ACTB-related second case; the first ACTG1 case was diagnosed with DFNA20/26 and is not used
      as BRWS treatment evidence.
  - reference: PMID:38592426
    reference_title: 'Hearing Loss in Baraitser-Winter Syndrome: Case Reports and Review of the Literature.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: >-
      Speech perception with right CI and left HA: 100% of intelligibility at 50 dB
    explanation: >-
      This is an aided speech-perception result, not complete normalization of language.
  - reference: PMID:38592426
    reference_title: 'Hearing Loss in Baraitser-Winter Syndrome: Case Reports and Review of the Literature.'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: >-
      intelligibility of spontaneous production remains poor.
    explanation: >-
      Residual functional communication limitation remained.
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: Cochlear implantation

      label: Surgical Procedure

    and 20/50 left to 25/25 in both eyes over three years. The maculae were spared by the colobomata, limiting
    generalization to other ocular anatomy.
  action_category: THERAPEUTIC

    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    snippet: >-
      For amblyopia treatment, glasses were prescribed for full correction, and occlusion therapy was started
      for the left eye. After 3 years of regular follow-up after the initial diagnosis, the patient’s visual
      acuity had improved to 25/25 in both eyes.
    explanation: >-

- name: Genetic Counseling
  description: >-
    Offer parental testing and counseling about autosomal dominant inheritance. Most cases are de novo, but
    parental germline mosaicism can cause recurrence despite negative parental blood testing. Each child of
    an affected individual has a 50% chance of inheriting the variant. Prenatal and preimplantation testing
    are possible once the familial variant is known.
  action_category: COUNSELING_INFORMATIONAL
  evidence:
  - reference: url:https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK327153/pdf/Bookshelf_NBK327153.pdf
    reference_title: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK327153/pdf/Bookshelf_NBK327153.pdf
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: >-
      Molecular genetic testing is recommended for the parents of the proband to evaluate their genetic status
      and inform recurrence risk assessment.
    explanation: >-
      GeneReviews (March 2022 revision): Parental testing informs recurrence counseling.
  - reference: url:https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK327153/pdf/Bookshelf_NBK327153.pdf
    reference_title: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK327153/pdf/Bookshelf_NBK327153.pdf
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: >-
      Testing of parental leukocyte DNA may not detect all instances of somatic mosaicism and will not detect
      a pathogenic variant that is present in the germ cells only.
    explanation: >-
      GeneReviews (March 2022 revision): A negative blood test does not exclude germline mosaicism.
  - reference: url:https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK327153/pdf/Bookshelf_NBK327153.pdf
    reference_title: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK327153/pdf/Bookshelf_NBK327153.pdf
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: >-
      Each child of an individual with BWCFF syndrome has a 50% chance of inheriting the ACTB or ACTG1 pathogenic
      variant.
    explanation: >-
      GeneReviews (March 2022 revision): The 50% risk applies to offspring of an affected heterozygote.
  - reference: url:https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK327153/pdf/Bookshelf_NBK327153.pdf
    reference_title: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK327153/pdf/Bookshelf_NBK327153.pdf
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: >-
      Once the ACTB or ACTG1 pathogenic variant has been identified in an affected family member, prenatal
      and preimplantation genetic testing for BWCFF syndrome are possible.
    explanation: >-
      GeneReviews (March 2022 revision): Reproductive testing requires identification of the familial variant.
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: Genetic Counseling
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15240
      label: Genetic Counseling
- name: Developmental and Organ Surveillance
  description: >-
    Monitor development and educational needs at each visit. Follow seizures as clinically indicated. Provide
    at least annual ophthalmology with glaucoma screening when coloboma or microphthalmia is present, annual
    assessment of hearing-loss progression, and at least annual review of feeding/GI dysfunction and scoliosis.
    Orthopedic review increases to every six months during growth spurts and adolescence; cardiac and renal
    follow-up depend on existing anomalies.
  action_category: MONITORING
  evidence:

    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: >-
      If coloboma or microphthalmia present, ophthalmologic follow up w/ screening for intraocular hypertension

    explanation: >-

    reference_title: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK327153/pdf/Bookshelf_NBK327153.pdf
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS

    reference_title: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK327153/pdf/Bookshelf_NBK327153.pdf
